meaning.en: To enjoy a delicious feast.
meaning.zh: 指吃到了好吃的东西，满足了口腹之欲。

equivalents: a treat for the taste buds

examples.zh: 这次去成都，我大饱口福。
examples.en: On this trip to Chengdu, I ate like a king.

examples.zh: 妈妈做了一桌好菜，让我们大饱口福。
examples.en: Mum cooked a feast, a real treat for our taste buds.

usage.en: Predicate. Modelled on 大饱眼福.

meaning.en: To study diligently in great poverty.
meaning.zh: 形容生活清苦，刻苦读书。

examples.zh: 范仲淹少时断齑画粥，刻苦攻读。
examples.en: As a youth Fan Zhongyan lived on divided porridge and chopped pickles while studying hard.

examples.zh: 他断齑画粥，终于学有所成。
examples.en: Studying in poverty, he eventually succeeded.

story.en: The young Fan Zhongyan, studying in a temple, cooked a pot of porridge each evening, let it set, cut it into four pieces, and ate two pieces morning and evening with a few chopped pickles.
story.zh: 范仲淹少年时在寺中读书，每天煮一锅粥，凝固后划成四块，早晚各吃两块，再切些咸菜佐食。

meaning.en: To destroy rivals by setting them against each other.
meaning.zh: 比喻借刀杀人，用计谋使人相互残杀。

equivalents: set them at each other's throats

examples.zh: 他用了二桃杀三士的计谋，让对手互相争斗。
examples.en: He set his rivals against each other, divide and rule.

examples.zh: 二桃杀三士的故事说明了计谋的厉害。
examples.en: The story of two peaches and three warriors shows the power of cunning.

story.en: The minister Yanzi had the Duke of Qi offer two peaches to three arrogant warriors, to be shared by merit. Each argued, then in shame killed himself.
story.zh: 晏子让齐景公赐给三位骄横的勇士两个桃子，让他们论功取桃。三人争功后又羞愧自杀。

meaning.en: A perfect partnership of planner and decision-maker.
meaning.zh: 房玄龄善于谋划，杜如晦善于决断。比喻同心协力，各有所长。

examples.zh: 两位创始人房谋杜断，配合默契。
examples.en: The two founders are a dream team — one plans, the other decides.

examples.zh: 他们俩一个出主意一个拍板，堪称房谋杜断。
examples.en: One comes up with ideas, the other makes the call — perfect partners.

story.en: Emperor Taizong's ministers Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were famous partners: "Xuanling was good at planning, Ruhui at deciding."
story.zh: 唐太宗时房玄龄、杜如晦同心辅政，"玄龄善谋，如晦能断"。

natural: A flying bear entering the dream

meaning.en: An omen of finding a great talent to help one rule.
meaning.zh: 比喻圣主得贤臣的征兆。

examples.zh: 周文王飞熊入梦，访得姜太公。
examples.en: King Wen dreamt of a flying bear and found Jiang Ziya.

examples.zh: 老板说遇到他就像飞熊入梦。
examples.en: The boss said finding him was like a dream come true.

story.en: Before hunting, King Wen of Zhou divined that he would catch "not a dragon, not a tiger, not a bear" but a helper of kings — and met Jiang Ziya fishing by the Wei River. Later tellings made it a dream of a flying bear.
story.zh: 周文王出猎前占卜，得"所获非龙非彲，非虎非罴，所获霸王之辅"，果然在渭水边遇到姜太公。后世演化为"飞熊入梦"。

meaning.en: Thriving and flourishing (of a business or career).
meaning.zh: 形容事情做得特别好，蓬勃兴旺。

examples.zh: 他的生意越做越风生水起。
examples.en: His business is booming.

examples.zh: 这家公司在新领域做得风生水起。
examples.en: The company is going great guns in the new field.

usage.en: Predicate or complement (做得风生水起). Modern popular usage.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、补语，现代常用。

natural: A Buddha's mouth and a snake's heart

meaning.en: Sweet words hiding a vicious heart.
meaning.zh: 佛的嘴巴，蛇的心肠。比喻嘴上说得好听，心肠却很狠毒。

examples.zh: 他佛口蛇心，别被他的好话骗了。
examples.en: He's a wolf in sheep's clothing — don't be fooled by his sweet talk.

examples.zh: 这个人佛口蛇心，害了不少人。
examples.en: This honey-tongued villain has harmed many.

meaning.en: Legendary swords; a peerless blade.
meaning.zh: 古代传说中的两把宝剑名，也是铸剑夫妇的名字。泛指宝剑。

examples.zh: 干将莫邪是传说中最锋利的宝剑。
examples.en: Ganjiang and Moye are the sharpest swords of legend.

examples.zh: 这把刀可谓干将莫邪。
examples.en: This blade is a peerless one.

story.en: The swordsmith Ganjiang and his wife Moye forged a pair of swords for the King of Wu; when the metal wouldn't fuse, Moye cut her hair and nails into the furnace. The swords were named after them.
story.zh: 干将与妻子莫邪为吴王铸剑，金铁不熔，莫邪剪下头发指甲投入炉中，铸成雌雄二剑，以二人名字命名。

natural: Tall buildings standing like a forest

meaning.en: A forest of skyscrapers.
meaning.zh: 高楼像树林一样密集地矗立着。

examples.zh: 如今这里高楼林立，十年前还是农田。
examples.en: It's a forest of skyscrapers now; ten years ago it was farmland.

examples.zh: 高楼林立的城市让人感到压抑。
examples.en: A concrete jungle can feel oppressive.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. A descriptive 四字词语 common in news.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，新闻常用。

natural: Master Zhou who turns at a wrong note

meaning.en: A connoisseur of music.
meaning.zh: 指精通音乐、戏曲的人。

examples.zh: 他是戏曲界的顾曲周郎。
examples.en: He's a true connoisseur of opera.

examples.zh: 在座都是顾曲周郎，我就献丑了。
examples.en: Everyone here has a discerning ear, but I'll do my best.

story.en: The general Zhou Yu was so musical that even after drinks, if a player made a mistake he would turn to look — people said: "If the tune is wrong, Master Zhou turns his head" (曲有误，周郎顾).
story.zh: 周瑜精通音乐，酒过三巡后仍能听出错误，必回头看，时人谣曰："曲有误，周郎顾。"

natural: A noble house as deep as the sea

meaning.en: The gulf between the powerful and ordinary people; lost to the world of the rich.
meaning.zh: 王公贵族的门庭像大海一样深。比喻旧时相识的人，因地位悬殊而疏远隔绝。

equivalents: a gulf between rich and poor

examples.zh: 侯门似海，她嫁入豪门后就再没见过老朋友。
examples.en: After marrying into wealth, she was lost to her old friends.

examples.zh: 一入侯门深似海。
examples.en: Once through the noble gate, it's as deep as the sea.

story.en: Cui Jiao's beloved maid was sold to a powerful official. He wrote: "Once through the noble's gate it is deep as the sea; from now on Master Xiao is a stranger on the road."
story.zh: 崔郊心爱的婢女被卖给权贵，他写诗："侯门一入深如海，从此萧郎是路人。"

natural: Drawing a tiger that looks like a dog

meaning.en: An overambitious imitation that fails ridiculously.
meaning.zh: 画老虎不成，反倒像狗。比喻模仿得不到家，反而弄得不伦不类。

examples.zh: 模仿大师的风格要谨慎，否则画虎类犬。
examples.en: Be careful imitating a master, or you'll end up with a botched copy.

examples.zh: 他学人家的演讲风格，结果画虎类犬。
examples.en: He copied someone's speaking style and it came out ridiculous.

origin.source: 东汉·马援《诫兄子严敦书》

story.en: General Ma Yuan warned his nephews not to imitate the flamboyant Du Ji: "If you try to draw a tiger and fail, it ends up looking like a dog."
story.zh: 马援写信告诫侄子不要学杜季良："效季良不得，陷为天下轻薄子，所谓画虎不成反类狗者也。"

usage.en: Predicate. Also 画虎不成反类犬.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。也作"画虎不成反类犬"。

natural: All over the body, top to bottom

meaning.en: From head to toe; all over.
meaning.zh: 整个身体，全身。

examples.zh: 他淋了雨，浑身上下都湿透了。
examples.en: Caught in the rain, he was soaked from head to toe.

examples.zh: 她浑身上下都是名牌。
examples.en: She's in designer labels from top to bottom.

natural: Waving a halberd to turn back the sun

meaning.en: To turn back the tide; to reverse a hopeless situation.
meaning.zh: 挥动长戈使太阳退回。比喻排除困难，扭转危局。

examples.zh: 他力图挥戈反日，挽救公司。
examples.en: He tried to turn back the tide and save the company.

examples.zh: 在最后时刻，球队挥戈反日，逆转获胜。
examples.en: At the last moment the team turned the tide and won.

story.en: Lord Luyang was fighting at dusk; he waved his halberd at the setting sun and it moved back three lunar mansions.
story.zh: 鲁阳公与韩国交战，天色将晚，他挥戈指向太阳，太阳竟退回了三个星宿的距离。

natural: A discerning eye that spots the pearl

meaning.en: To have an eye for talent or value.
meaning.zh: 比喻能够识别人才或好东西。

equivalents: spot a diamond in the rough

examples.zh: 多亏老板慧眼识珠，他才有了发挥的机会。
examples.en: Thanks to the boss's eye for talent, he got his chance.

examples.zh: 这位收藏家慧眼识珠，发现了一件国宝。
examples.en: The collector's discerning eye spotted a national treasure.

meaning.en: Win-win; mutually beneficial.
meaning.zh: 互相带来利益，共同取得成功。

examples.zh: 两国合作实现了互利共赢。
examples.en: The two countries' cooperation produced a win-win outcome.

examples.zh: 我们追求互利共赢的伙伴关系。
examples.en: We seek mutually beneficial partnerships.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. A modern diplomatic and business set phrase.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。现代外交、商务常用语。

natural: Counting the days to measure progress

meaning.en: Success is just around the corner; steady, measurable progress.
meaning.zh: 工作进度或成功日期可以按日计算。形容进展快，成功在望。

examples.zh: 工程进展顺利，竣工计日程功。
examples.en: The project is going smoothly; completion is within sight.

examples.zh: 只要坚持下去，成功可以计日程功。
examples.en: If we keep going, success is just a matter of time.

meaning.en: As strong as an ox.
meaning.zh: 身体像牛一样健壮。

examples.zh: 他每天锻炼，健壮如牛。
examples.en: He works out every day and is as strong as an ox.

examples.zh: 别看爷爷七十了，还健壮如牛。
examples.en: Grandpa may be seventy, but he's still as strong as an ox.

usage.en: Predicate. Same image as the English idiom.

meaning.en: To speak too frankly to a slight acquaintance.
meaning.zh: 跟交情浅的人说心里话。

examples.zh: 我们刚认识，交浅言深，请别见怪。
examples.en: We've only just met, so forgive me if I'm too frank.

examples.zh: 职场上要避免交浅言深。
examples.en: At work, avoid oversharing with people you barely know.

usage.en: Predicate. Often as a polite disclaimer before speaking frankly.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常作直言前的谦辞。

literal: tie · grass · hold in mouth · ring
natural: Tying grass and carrying jade rings

meaning.en: To repay a kindness even after death.
meaning.zh: 比喻感恩图报，至死不忘。

equivalents: repay a debt even in death

examples.zh: 您的大恩大德，我结草衔环也难以报答。
examples.en: I could never repay your great kindness even beyond the grave.

examples.zh: 他发誓要结草衔环，报答恩人。
examples.en: He vowed to repay his benefactor forever.

origin.source: 《左传·宣公十五年》；《后汉书·杨震传》注引《续齐谐记》

story.en: An old man's ghost tied grass to trip the enemy of Wei Ke, who had spared his daughter. A yellow bird healed by young Yang Bao returned as a boy bearing four white jade rings in thanks.
story.zh: 魏颗未让父妾殉葬，后来作战时，妾父的鬼魂结草绊倒敌将以报恩。杨宝救了一只黄雀，黄雀化为童子衔白环四枚相报。

meaning.en: Carefree, extravagant indulgence in drink.
meaning.zh: 拿官帽上的金貂换酒喝。形容不拘礼法、纵情饮酒。

examples.zh: 他效仿古人金貂换酒，纵情山水。
examples.en: He drank and roamed without a care, like the ancients.

examples.zh: 金貂换酒的故事表现了魏晋名士的洒脱。
examples.en: The story shows the free spirit of the Wei-Jin literati.

story.en: The official Ruan Fu once traded the golden sable ornament from his official cap for wine; he was impeached but pardoned.
story.zh: 阮孚曾以官帽上的金貂换酒，被人弹劾，皇帝宽宥了他。

meaning.en: To make a terrain model to plan strategy; a clear analysis of the situation.
meaning.zh: 用米堆成山川地形。比喻指画形势，运筹决策。

equivalents: a clear picture of the battlefield

examples.zh: 他聚米为山，向将军们讲解作战计划。
examples.en: He built a model of the terrain to explain the battle plan.

examples.zh: 规划师聚米为山，展示了新城区的蓝图。
examples.en: The planner laid out a model to show the new district's blueprint.

story.en: General Ma Yuan piled up rice before Emperor Guangwu to model the mountains and valleys of the enemy's territory, explaining the campaign so clearly the emperor said: "The enemy is in my sight."
story.zh: 马援在光武帝面前"聚米为山谷，指画形势"，光武帝说："虏在吾目中矣。"

natural: Harsh government is fiercer than a tiger

meaning.en: Oppressive government is worse than a man-eating tiger.
meaning.zh: 残酷压迫人民的政治比吃人的老虎还要凶猛。

equivalents: tyranny is worse than any beast

examples.zh: 苛政猛于虎，百姓宁可住在深山。
examples.en: Oppression is fiercer than tigers — people would rather live in the wild mountains.

examples.zh: 这个故事告诉我们苛政猛于虎。
examples.en: The story teaches that tyranny is worse than any beast.

story.en: Confucius met a woman weeping at a grave: tigers had killed her father-in-law, husband and son. Asked why she didn't leave, she said: "There is no harsh government here." Confucius said: "Remember — harsh government is fiercer than a tiger."
story.zh: 孔子遇到一妇人哭墓，她的公公、丈夫、儿子都被老虎咬死，问她为何不离开，答："无苛政。"孔子说："小子识之，苛政猛于虎也。"

meaning.en: To pursue (or hurry) through the night without stopping.
meaning.zh: 当夜就连续不停地追赶。

examples.zh: 警察连夜追赶逃犯。
examples.en: The police pursued the fugitive through the night.

examples.zh: 为了完成订单，工人们连夜追赶进度。
examples.en: To fill the order, the workers raced through the night to catch up.

usage.en: Predicate. A narrative 四字词语 common in stories and news.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常见于叙事和新闻。

meaning.en: As bright as day (of lighting at night).
meaning.zh: 明亮得像白天一样。

examples.zh: 晚会现场灯火通明，亮如白昼。
examples.en: The gala venue was lit up as bright as day.

examples.zh: 满月之夜，院子里亮如白昼。
examples.en: On the night of the full moon, the courtyard was as bright as day.

usage.en: Predicate. A descriptive 四字词语.
